# PROCESS — what I did this iteration (explainability; REQUIRED)

Candidate cand_0002 (iteration 2/3). The parent is cand_0001 at val 0.800 (32/40). Eight tasks fail: 51-12, 267-18, 227-40, 402-43, 45635, 50768, 43436, 48527. cand_0001 broke two of them, 402-43 and 45635 (LEDGER).

Method:
- I read all 8 failing trajectories and compared each output with the gold workbook, to classify the failure only. No values were copied.
- I dumped every init workbook to see in-sheet examples, labels and formulas, and checked the seed rollouts of 402-43/45635 to see why they passed before.
- I read the adapter's `_extract_python` and confirmed that only the FIRST ```python block of a reply executes. I also confirmed that the adapter does not `.format()` prompt.md (`_read_system_prompt` reads it raw), so braces in prompt.md are safe.

## Ranked issue list (clusters by # failing tasks, biggest first)
| rank | cluster | tasks | shared root cause | tag | planned change class |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | F. In-sheet examples present but not reconciled | 48527 (pre-filled D2/D3 contradict the literal rule; the agent noticed and kept the literal rule), 51-12 (row-2 marker numbers mark the hit cells; the agent got 2 vs 4), 43436 (neighbouring H column has a working COUNTIFS per department; the agent did per-record flags), 227-40 (expected block keeps blanks in place; the agent compacted) | cand_0001 says "treat examples as the spec" but has no step that FORCES computing the rule on the example cells and comparing, so the agent never sees a mismatch. | BEHAVIORAL | ordered procedure (2a list examples → 2c reconcile computed-vs-existing; examples beat literal wording) |
| 2 | G. Answer cells mapped to the wrong entity/axis | 50768 (grid axes swapped; the pre-filled cell would have shown it), 45635 (score is per column among persons; the agent went per row), 43436 (row labels = departments) | The agent never reads the labels beside the answer cells or which axis is which. | BEHAVIORAL | ordered step 2b "labels: both axes, confirm with pre-filled cell, same-label mapping, the comparison set follows what is shared" |
| 3 | H. Partial inspection hides the spec | 227-40 (printed only to row 11 and missed the full block), 402-43 (missed that rows 14+ are a "would become" example with a header row), 51-12 (ignored row 2) | Ad-hoc inspection prints a few chosen cells, so example blocks and labels are missed. | BEHAVIORAL / KNOWLEDGE | worked example: a fixed round-1 dump script (all non-empty cells, cached value + formula, bounded output) |
| 4 | I. Table outputs: header row omitted / shape changed | 402-43 (gold Sheet2 row 1 = header; the agent wrote data only), 227-40 (blank cells shifted left) | No rule on table shape. The seed passed 402-43 via to_excel's default header, and cand_0001's openpyxl rule lost that header. | KNOWLEDGE | explicit contract: the source table ends at the first blank row; a new sheet/region starts with the header row; copy the example shape, with blanks kept in place |
| 5 | J. Untouched formula cells in answer_position read as None | 267-18 (G1 left as a formula → None; only G2 changed) | openpyxl save drops cached values for ALL formula cells, and the agent can't know this. | KNOWLEDGE | sourced rule + reason (graded rule 2) + example line |
| 6 | K. Float threshold | 51-12 (`110 >= 100*1.1` is False in its code) | Python float representation | KNOWLEDGE | rule + concrete numeric example |
| 7 | L. Multi-block replies | 45635 (5 blocks in one reply), 48527 (4); later blocks never ran, wasting rounds | The adapter runs only the first block, and the agent doesn't know this. | KNOWLEDGE | "## Rounds" contract sentence + template line |

## Changes made this iteration (one row per edit)
| cluster | edit class | file | what & why it generalizes | protects passing? |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| F | restructure into ordered procedure (6) | prompt.md workflow 2a/2c; task_template.md steps 2–3 | List the example cells; placeholders (`n/a`, `?`, blank) are NOT examples. Run the rule on the examples, print computed vs existing, and change the rule until all match. | Pre-fills in passing tasks (9569, 12864, 48921) are consistent with gold, so reconciling leaves the answer unchanged. 59595's 'n/a' cells are explicitly excluded. |
| G | add rule (4) | prompt.md workflow 2b | Read labels on both axes, confirm with a pre-filled cell, map same labels to each other. The comparison set is what the instruction says is shared ("each column is worth N" → compare down the column). | Additive. Passing labelled-grid tasks already map correctly. |
| H | add worked example (5) | prompt.md workflow 1 (dump script) | Fixed round-1 inspection. Tested on all 40 init workbooks: max ~7.5 KB output; 80-42 ~32 KB (row-capped at 30 per sheet / 120 total); ≤3 s; no errors. | Read-only; it replaces only the agent's ad-hoc inspection. |
| I | tighten output contract (8) | prompt.md workflow 4 "Table-shaped outputs" | The source table is header + rows down to the first blank row. A table on a new/empty sheet starts with the header. The example shape is copied, with blanks kept in place. | 395-36 (new sheet, header in row 1) and 560-12 (header placed per instruction; "unless the example block or instruction shows otherwise") stay consistent. |
| J | sourced rule + reason (4, 2) + example (5) | prompt.md graded rule 2; example `elif` line; task_template.md step 3; verify step | Every formula cell inside answer_position becomes a literal (its cached value if unchanged). | 48620, 53647, 55049, 56563, 6698, 7902, 9726, 382-10 already overwrite all such cells. 382-10 A18 has cached None = gold None, so it is unchanged. |
| K | add rule with concrete example (4, 5) | prompt.md workflow 3 last bullet | `cur >= ref*1.1 - 1e-9` | Only affects exact-boundary comparisons. |
| L | tighten interaction contract (8) | prompt.md "## Rounds"; task_template.md round line | Only the first block runs, so use one block per round. | Passing traces already use one block. |

## Verify-the-fix (trace → what the new text does on those inputs)
- 48527: the trace says the pre-filled D2=Apple/D3=Orange "contradict" the rule, then keeps the literal rule. Step 2c now says a mismatch means the reading is wrong: change the rule until ALL examples match. The gold rule, the value occurring once in A:C, reproduces D2/D3.
- 51-12: the trace's code (`if current_val >= ref_val * 1.1`) gave 2. With the tolerance, 110 ≥ 110 counts. The row-2 markers (C2=1, E2=2, H2=3, L2=4) are now listed examples ("marker numbers placed next to the data"), and reconciling against them gives 4.
- 43436: H2:H6 holds `=COUNTIFS(B:B,G2,D:D,"")`, one per department label in G. The dump shows the formula in brackets. Steps 2a/2b say a neighbouring formula column and the row labels define each answer row, so the output is per-department counts, not per-record flags.
- 227-40: the expected block in rows 9–12 keeps None in place. The dump prints the whole block, and rule 4 says blanks stay at their position (no left shift). The header at row 14 stays as in cand_0001's output.
- 402-43: the dump shows the table in rows 1–7, a blank gap, then A14 "THE ABOVE TABLE WOULD BECOME:" with a header at row 16 (verified by running the script). Rule 4 says the source ends at the first blank row and a new sheet starts with the header row, which matches gold Sheet2 row 1 = header.
- 45635: the dump shows A1:A3 = A/B/C and A5:A7 = A/B/C. Via 2b, the instruction "The columns each represent 6 points" means compare down each column, and same-label mapping gives B5 ← B1. This matches gold `IF(B1=MAX(B$1:B$3),6/COUNTIF(...))`.
- 50768: the grid axes are E12:E14 (Impact) and F15:H15 (Likelihood), with F14 = '1, 3, 5' pre-filled. 2b requires reading both axes and confirming with the pre-filled cell, so swapped axes fail the reconcile check.
- 267-18: the dump shows formulas in both G1 and G2 (verified by running the script). Graded rule 2 says G1 is overwritten too, with its cached value; gold G1 = cached value.
- Template validity: `string.Formatter().parse` on the new template returns exactly the 6 required fields + max_turns, and `.format()` with 7 keys renders (checked). The dump script extracted from prompt.md ran without error on 267-18, 227-40, 43436 and 80-42.

## Blast radius (passing tasks)
- Dump script: read-only, runs on all 40 init files without error, with bounded output. The only risk is extra context on 80-42 (32 KB, capped).
- Reconcile step: tasks with pre-filled cells (9569, 12864, 48921) are consistent with gold. 59595's 'n/a' placeholders are explicitly "not examples".
- Formula-to-literal rule: see the J row.
- Table rule: 395-36 and 560-12 stay consistent, and "unless the example block or instruction shows otherwise" keeps instruction-specified placement. The plain-table passes (9726, 382-10, 12864, 142-12, 2768) write into existing layouts, not onto a new headerless sheet.
- Float tolerance: affects only exact-boundary comparisons.
- Prompt length: ~4.7 KB → ~8.5 KB system prompt. Gemma context is ample.

## Process & features used
- Subagents / worktrees / parallel features used: none. This was serial in-context analysis, because the session instructions say not to call Agent/Workflow unless the user requests it.
- Prior iterations read: prior_iterations/cand_0001 (PROCESS + diff), LEDGER (broke 402-43, 45635), rejected.jsonl (empty).

## Good things to PRESERVE
- cand_0001's literal-values grading contract, openpyxl edit-in-place, and verify→DONE ending (+0.350).
- The placeholder contract in task_template.md.

## Deliberately skipped
- No adapter/scorer/environment change. No task-specific values: the dump script and example use generic placeholders (`Sheet1`, `<spreadsheet_path>`).
- I did not soften the to_excel rule to recover 402-43. Its seed pass came from to_excel's default header, so the explicit header-row rule addresses it without reopening layout-destruction cluster B.
